heading: About
body: I own architecture and performance on large codebases, and run the code review that keeps them maintainable. Most of what I ship is infrastructure other teams build on: low-code platforms, back-office systems, document management, e-commerce. React, Next.js and TypeScript on the front, Node.js and PostgreSQL behind it, with LLM features in the recent products.

language.short: Designed the DSL behind a low-code reporting platform, so analysts could write their own formulas instead of filing tickets.
language.detail: Grammar, editor and evaluation: a parser built with Chevrotain and Lezer, wired into a CodeMirror editor with completion and inline errors.

clients.short: Worked directly with clients in the EU and the US, with no manager in between.
clients.detail: Contract work, not a staff role.

platform.short: Owned the frontend architecture of that platform: a widget system configured at runtime.
platform.detail: Every table, chart and text block is defined by the user, over data read from their own databases, with undo/redo, archive creation and PDF export on top.

payments.short: Built payments and subscriptions from the store receipt through to the renewal job.
payments.detail: Receipt verification, webhooks, background jobs for renewal and expiry, and PostgreSQL access rules with logging that never writes a token.

ai.short: Took LLM features from prototype to production, inside real product flows, not a demo chatbot.
ai.detail: Retrieval over the product's own documents, streaming responses, tool calling and agent-style flows, routed through OpenRouter rather than tied to a single vendor.

performance.short: Kept large tables and charts responsive on codebases too large for one engineer to hold in full context.
performance.detail: Virtualised the big tables, split and lazy-loaded the routes, trimmed the bundle, and cut repeat GraphQL round trips with fragment-level caching.

review.short: Set up the code review process, and mentored the developers who joined after.
review.detail: Wrote the specs the code was built from, and the shared AI coding rules and prompts the team worked to.

personal: Most of my career has been remote, working with German, American, Israeli and Ukrainian teams. The same sentence carries different weight depending on who says it: direct feedback that is normal in one team reads as rudeness in another. Erin Meyer's "The Culture Map" is good on this. Knowing that early stops you reading a blunt sentence as a personal problem.
I like difficult problems and play too much Dark Souls. My approach to both is the same: understand how something works before trying harder.
Outside work: manga, long walks and tea. Tea is the only skill on my LinkedIn that was endorsed without me asking.
